# ADR-0034 §2.3 item 10: the setup effect runs through the shared orchestration

## Context

ADR-0034 §2.3 item 10 (added by #19366) records the first-run setup broker's six capabilities. Its `setupEffect` bullet describes the state on 2026-10-02: *"As recorded here, the handler refuses every call by name (`unwired: …`)"*, with the wiring named as neomjs/neo-agent-institution#440's. That leaf merged on 2026-10-03 (neomjs/neo-agent-institution#464), so the sentence is history. The follow-up was declared in that PR's body and confirmed in its review.

## The Problem

The record now contradicts the shipped shell in three places of one bullet and one sentence of the custody paragraph:

- the handler no longer refuses every call: it runs the one consented effect through the Brain's shared orchestration;
- the refusal name `unwired` no longer exists in the shell or in the card;
- the card's row is no longer the operator's instruction for every refusal: a refusal in the orchestration's words stays on the status line, and only a shell that cannot run effects at all hands the operator the CLI;
- the custody paragraph does not say what the broker does after a record write the host rejected.

A reader who implements against the record would re-introduce the manual path.

## The Architectural Reality

- `learn/agentos/decisions/0034-electron-shell-architecture.md`, §2.3 item 10: the `setupEffect` bullet and the **Custody** paragraph.
- The shipped contract (Institution `dev@424fa0e`, `harness/setupBroker.mjs`): `effect` = the settle pass, then `performEffects` for the one named effect in the recipe's order rules, then the re-evaluated run, as one serialized operation; a refusal reported by the orchestration answers `{ok: false, reason, effectId}` and writes nothing; a boot without a Brain root refuses `no-brain-root`. The broker holds the run's record path only and reads the record from disk in every operation; a bound record that is gone or unreadable refuses the operation.
- ADR 0041 §2 item 6 (an interrupted effect is settled by observation, never replayed) is the authority the custody sentence leans on.

## The Fix

1. The `setupEffect` bullet states the wired contract: what runs, the two refusal shapes, and that no second implementation of the effects exists in main. The dated "as recorded here" sentence and the `unwired` name go.
2. The **Custody** paragraph gains one sentence: every record operation starts from the record on disk, so an effect whose acknowledgement write was rejected is found `pending` and settled by observation; a record the broker cannot read refuses the operation.
3. The item's amendment note names this leaf and its date.

## Decision Record impact

amends ADR-0034 §2.3 item 10 (documentation of a shipped contract; no new capability, no change to the six channels' names or envelopes).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 The `setupEffect` bullet describes the wired handler and its refusals; neither `unwired` nor "refuses every call" remains in the record.
- [ ] AC-2 The Custody paragraph states the read-from-disk rule and the unreadable-record refusal.
- [ ] AC-3 The item's amendment note carries this leaf and 2026-10-03.

## Out of Scope

A `fresh` flag on `setupEvaluate` (neomjs/neo-agent-institution#475): its own amendment, ahead of that leaf, if it ships.
